key_insight: Menopause is linked to distinct blood-protein changes that resemble accelerated brain aging and may help explain later dementia risk.
clinical_relevance: These protein patterns could eventually support biomarker development or treatment targeting to protect cognitive health in midlife women.
method: Measured serum proteomics in 80 carefully staged pre-, peri-, and postmenopausal women.
Validated findings in 2,814 age-matched women using plasma proteomics.
Tested associations in four independent older-women cohorts with cognitive outcomes.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports replicated proteomic shifts across cohorts and consistent associations with poorer cognition in 11,925 older women.
watch_item: Associations do not prove causation, and the findings will need longitudinal and mechanistic validation before clinical use.
paper_title: Blood proteomics of menopause map to brain aging and dementia risk
